message.content: {"distractor_2":"Run dbt run-operation generate_model_yaml -m models/core/activity_based_interest --args '{upstream_descriptions: True}' and then run dbt docs generate to build the docs","explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_2":"This is wrong because dbt run-operation macros (like generate_model_yaml) do not accept the model selector (-m) to target models. The macro expects an explicit model_names list (or you must programmatically supply names via dbt ls), so relying on the selector means no models will be passed to the macro and the YAML won't be generated as intended.","thinking_process_2":"I assumed dbt's selector flags (-m) could be applied to any dbt command the same way they are to dbt run or dbt test, so using -m with run-operation would conveniently target the directory. However, run-operation is for executing macros and doesn't interpret model selectors; you must supply model names through the macro arguments (e.g., from dbt ls) rather than using -m."}

{"distractor_2":"Create a single staging model that ingests all three source systems, applies universal column renames, type normalization, and null handling, and performs the cross-source joins to produce a consolidated customer table","explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_2":"This is wrong because it lumps source-specific cleaning and cross-source logic into one model. Combining all sources in a single staging model creates tight coupling between sources, makes it hard to test and reason about source-specific transformations, increases blast radius when one source changes, and prevents reusing clean, canonical views of each source in downstream models. The correct dbt pattern is to keep one staging model per source (isolated, testable canonical representations) and perform joins in explicit downstream transformations.","thinking_process_2":"I crafted a plausible-sounding alternative that some teams use to simplify pipeline structure — one consolidated staging model that does everything. It follows the same surface pattern (column renames, type normalization, null handling) but applies them across all sources at once. I highlighted the conceptual mistake (wrong architectural approach: coupling and lack of isolation) rather than a wrong technology, to meet the requirement of using the right tools but the wrong method."}
